The larger the difference in electronegativity between two atoms, the more ionic the bond is. Covalent bonds, on the other hand, have smaller differences in electronegativity.

We can qualitatively assess the ionic character of the bonds in each molecule as follows :

- : Both nitrogen atoms have the same electronegativity since it is a diatomic molecule of the same element, therefore the bond is purely covalent with no ionic character.

- : Sulfur and oxygen have different electronegativities, with oxygen being more electronegative than sulfur, but not as drastically different as in ionic compounds. Therefore, the bond has some ionic character but is primarily covalent.
